Vegas looks like the better side on paper, and the model has it scoring 3.40 expected goals tonight to Pittsburgh's 2.88. The gap is on defense. VGK allows 2.54 expected goals per 60 against PIT's 3.60, while the two create chances at a similar rate (3.55 for VGK, 3.39 for PIT). At five on five the teams are close, with PIT at 54% of the expected goals and VGK at 55%. Special teams lean Vegas too: its power play generates 0.94 expected goals per game and its penalty kill concedes 0.32, against 0.58 and 0.75 for Pittsburgh. VGK also draws 5.11 penalties per game.

Pittsburgh arrives on the second night of a back-to-back after a 2-5 loss in Denver. Sergei Murashov is the projected starter in net over Arturs Silovs, and the model prices both the schedule and the goalie change. Murashov sits at +0.69 goals saved above expected this season, and Carter Hart, the projected VGK starter, at +1.97. Last season they were at -3.52 in 5 games and -4.44 in 18 games. PIT is 1-3-1 in its last five with 46% of the expected goals, while VGK is 4-1-0 with 53%.

Mark Stone has the best scoring odds on the board at 36%, and he's a top power play option. Jack Eichel (31% to score, 72% to get a point) plays his 700th game, though the model doesn't price the milestone. For Pittsburgh, Sidney Crosby is at 30% to score, and Rickard Rakell is due after no goals in eight games on 2.7 expected goals. Egor Chinakhov could return for the Penguins as well.
